quotes.text: Traffic manager is a DNS-based load balancer that runs at global scale. Think of it like a smart reception desk at the entrance of a worldwide office building.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise definition with a memorable analogy for how Traffic Manager works.

quotes.text: Test your failover, actually simulate an outage and watch what happens. That's the only way to know it works.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, actionable advice against assuming a backup region will cope.

quotes.text: Weighted routing is not round robin. It doesn't alternate between endpoints one request at a time. It's a statistical distribution over a large number of requests.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a common misconception about weighted routing.

quotes.text: A better approach is to create a dedicated health check endpoint, something lightweight. A simple endpoint that returns a 200 status code quickly and confirms the application is running.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical best practice for reliable health probes.

quotes.text: Use traffic manager for cross-region routing. Use Azure Load Balancer for within region distribution. Use Front Door when you also need WAF caching and TLS termination at the edge.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A compact decision rule for choosing between Azure traffic services.

chapters.title: Decision guide: Traffic Manager vs. other options

takeaways: Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based global traffic director that never sits in the data path, so it adds no latency to user connections.

Its six routing methods cover different goals: priority for disaster recovery, performance for speed, weighted for canary releases, geographic for compliance, plus multi-value and subnet for niche cases.
Reliable failover depends on well-tuned health probes against a lightweight health endpoint and on regularly testing that backup regions can carry the full load.
hook: Users in Tokyo should not wait on a single server in Virginia, and one regional outage should not take your whole app offline. This episode explains Azure Traffic Manager for developers and cloud architects building multi-region apps: how DNS-based routing works, when to use each of its six routing methods, and how it fits alongside Load Balancer, Application Gateway and Front Door.
